The research names three vendor document models and chooses none: HubSpot renders an HTML/JSON document model in its quote editor and rasterises to PDF on publish; Dynamics 365 performs a Word content-control/XML merge against a schema beginning urn:microsoft-crm/document-template/; PandaDoc replaces content_placeholders with content library items at document creation. Which model should this workflow implement as its presentation layer?

state.problem: WF-093 builds a branded proposal by merging a template definition with quote record data. The research names three vendor document models and chooses none: HubSpot renders an HTML/JSON document model in its quote editor and rasterises to PDF on publish; Dynamics 365 performs a Word content-control/XML merge against a schema beginning urn:microsoft-crm/document-template/; PandaDoc replaces content_placeholders with content library items at document creation. candidate_solutions.html_json_document_model: HubSpot model. The merge produces an ordered JSON document model: a module list in template order, each module rendered from template bindings plus record data, plus a branding token block. Stored as the quote's presentation layer in records.data. No rendering runtime, no external schema, no content library. Honours the non-retroactive rule because the document is a stored snapshot, not a live view.
candidate_solutions.word_content_control_xml_merge: Dynamics model. The merge emits a Word document part with repeating content controls for 1:N line items and a 100-related-record cap per relationship. Requires carrying an entity XML schema the repository does not hold, and the cap becomes a real truncation rule this product would have to enforce.
candidate_solutions.pandadoc_content_placeholders: PandaDoc model. Template declares content_placeholders; each must be replaced with at least 1 and at most 10 content library items at creation time. Requires a content library collection this ticket does not claim, and makes every instantiation fail unless a library item exists for each placeholder.
candidate_solutions.store_all_three_as_declared_modes: Implement all three behind a mode field. Rejected here as the widest surface with three partial implementations, but Jev may select it if it believes the coverage is worth it.

context.constraint_no_shared_files: The feature may not edit dsr/api.py, dsr/store.py or components/ui.jsx, so nothing outside the feature's own files may grow to carry any of the three.
context.constraint_schema_flexible: Records are arbitrary JSON in records.data with a dynamic index. A JSON document model is a natural fit; a WordprocessingML part and its XML schema are not.
context.constraint_local_verifiable: The change must be verifiable over localhost with no vendor credential. The HTML/JSON model is fully derivable from the template and record data. A Word merge needs a schema file and a library store to be verifiable.
context.evidence_fixed_points: The evidence fixes: quote properties override template settings at merge; the template association is settable only at quote creation; template changes do not retro-apply to published quotes; custom coded modules cannot be created via the API. None of these four points distinguishes the three models.
context.repo_convention: Forty-plus features in this repository store their output as JSON in records.data and render it in a React page. No feature depends on a vendor document runtime.

A quote template definition (module order, hide/show, bindings, branding tokens) is merged

fixes. A published document refuses a re-render, because the research says a template or
branding change does not update a published quote.
